messages.author: 5b0c9158bfa781ba
messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] "subprocess failed with code 139"
parts:
Hello,
I figured out why. The RHIPE C program writes a startup message to a log file
/tmp/logger. Now I guess you ran some code first (and you can check permissions
as to who owns it : ls -l /tmp/logger) and then another person with a different
UID runs a mr job and RHIPE tries writing to this log files and fails.

So, you can
a) delete the log file (tedious)
b) download (yet again) from
http://ml.stat.purdue.edu/rhipe/dn/Rhipe_0.51.tar.gz

and install across the worker nodes. It should now work for both local
and non local jobs.

The new version creates a log file called /tmp/logger-UID where UID is the
effective UID of the user.

It should work now(tested with two different users, though for me Hadoop has
issues running local jobs for different users but I guess thats due to my
cranky setup)

BTW, every run adds a few lines to the log file (/tmp/logger-UID
replace UID with users UID) and does not perform any log rotation, so
after several jobs it might grow large ..(but hardly so)
Soon, I'll insert code for log rotation.
Regards
Saptarshi

messages.author: 5b0c9158bfa781ba
messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Re: "subprocess failed with code 139"
parts:
Hi

This is the first time other people are using my software, and if there
is one thing I have learned it is that different people have very
different environments from mine.

Thanks for your input, it can only improve RHIPE.

Regards
Saptarshi

----------
saptarshi guha | http://www.stat.purdue.edu/~sguha
One way to make your old car run better is to look up the price of a
new model.

On Wed, Dec 2, 2009 at 1:32 PM, ben.c...@lehman.com
<ben.c...@lehman.com> wrote:
>

> worked perfectly.  Thank you Saptarshi.  -Ben
>

> On Dec 2, 12:42 pm, Saptarshi Guha <saptarshi.g...@gmail.com> wrote:
>> Hello,
>> I figured out why. The RHIPE C program writes a startup message to a log file
>> /tmp/logger. Now I guess you ran some code first (and you can check permissions
>> as to who owns it : ls -l /tmp/logger) and then another person with a different
>> UID runs a mr job and RHIPE tries writing to this log files and fails.
>>
>> So, you can
>> a) delete the log file (tedious)
>> b) download (yet again) fromhttp://ml.stat.purdue.edu/rhipe/dn/Rhipe_0.51.tar.gz
>>
>> and install across the worker nodes. It should now work for both local
>> and non local jobs.
>>
>> The new version creates a log file called /tmp/logger-UID where UID is the
>> effective UID of the user.
>>
>> It should work now(tested with two different users, though for me Hadoop has
>> issues running local jobs for different users but I guess thats due to my
>> cranky setup)
>>
>> BTW, every run adds a few lines to the log file (/tmp/logger-UID
>> replace UID with users UID) and does not perform any log rotation, so
>> after several jobs it might grow large ..(but hardly so)
>> Soon, I'll insert code for log rotation.
>> Regards
>> Saptarshi
